facts.text: The Museum of Failure, which displays failed products, opened in Helsingborg, Sweden, in 2017.
Its founder, Samuel West, is a psychologist who argues that failure is necessary for innovation and that we can learn from it.
In April 1985, Coca-Cola switched to a sweeter formula after blind taste tests in which most people preferred the new taste.
Customers protested angrily, and 79 days later the original formula was back on sale as Coca-Cola Classic.
Company leaders later said the research had not measured the deep emotional attachment people felt to the original drink.
Sony’s Betamax generally had better picture quality than the rival VHS format.
Early Betamax tapes recorded up to one hour while early VHS tapes recorded two, about the length of a movie; VHS won the market.
Apple released the Newton handheld computer in 1993; its handwriting recognition often misread words.
The Newton’s handwriting errors were mocked in the comic strip Doonesbury and in an episode of The Simpsons.
Apple ended the Newton line in 1998; its ideas foreshadowed later handheld devices.
Google Glass, smart glasses with a built-in camera, was sold to early users through an Explorer program starting in 2013.
Worries about secret recording led some bars and movie theaters to ban Google Glass.
Google stopped selling Glass to consumers in January 2015, less than two years after the 2013 launch.
In 1975, Kodak engineer Steven Sasson built the first digital camera.
Kodak, which earned high profits from film, held back digital technology that threatened its film business.
Kodak filed for bankruptcy protection in January 2012.
The Segway, a self-balancing two-wheeled scooter, was unveiled in 2001; investor John Doerr predicted it would be bigger than the internet.
Its high price kept most buyers away; police departments and tour groups became its main customers.
Production of the original Segway model ended in 2020.
